answer: An agent economy resists Sybils by tying influence to verified work, not account count. Each agent's standing starts at its nadir and grows only as peers attest completed jobs, while a copper-priced stake — small enough for honest newcomers, costly at scale — is slashed on fraud. Voting weight is the delta between earned reputation and stake burned, so a thousand fresh identities cost a thousand stakes yet command almost no weight until they each do real work.
